Claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`. Branch: **`claude/issue-6316-docs-route-closure-gate`**. Assignee is this seat's shared identity — the claim is this comment plus the session ID.

⚠️ Note the routing: triage **re-routed this card `domain:ui` → `domain:devx`** because the fix is gate machinery in `scripts/`, not library code. You are building an instrument, not changing a renderer.

### The ruling you are executing (triage, 2026-08-25T18:07:49Z — verbatim)

> Triage: promoted `finding` → `pm:queue`, re-routed `domain:ui` → `domain:devx` (the fix is gate machinery in `scripts/`, not library code), type **Task**. Shape **2** is ruled as the dispatch: a structural gate asserting that every package named in `registerCatalogBlocks.ts` is already reachable from the docs route's existing graph — cheap, no 556-page CI build, and it converts "genuinely new graph" from an unmeasured hazard into an argued-for review event. Shape 1 (a second byte-budget site with its own ceiling) stays available as a follow-up if a legitimately new graph ever needs a real gauge — whoever hits the structural gate first files that card with the need in hand. Shape 3 is rejected: #4616's stop condition should not remain instrumentless when a cheap instrument exists.

⛔ **Shape 1 is closed for this card.** Do not add a docs-site build to CI, do not emit a second byte-budget report, do not introduce a new ceiling constant. The whole point of the ruling is that shape 2 costs no CI build.

### What you are building

A structural gate: **every package named in `apps/site/app/components/registerCatalogBlocks.ts` must already be reachable from the docs route's existing module graph.** A package that is already reachable adds a declaration and no payload; one that is not is a genuinely new graph, and the gate turns that into something a human argues for in review rather than something that lands unmeasured.

The card's worked example is the evidence this is the right shape: PR #6314 declared `@object-ui/plugin-form` and `@object-ui/plugin-grid`, and both were **already** in the route's eager closure via `@object-ui/plugin-view`'s module-scope `import { ObjectGrid }` / `import { ObjectForm }`. Your gate must pass on that case.

### The verification that decides whether this gate is real

⭐ **A structural gate that cannot fail is worse than no gate**, because it converts an unmeasured hazard into a false assurance. Prove both directions:

1. **Passes on the current tree**, unmodified.
2. **Fails when a genuinely unreachable package is named.** Plant one in `registerCatalogBlocks.ts`, run the gate, record **RED** with the message a reader would actually get. Restore via `git checkout HEAD -- <absolute path>` under a `trap … EXIT INT TERM`, prove the restore by `git hash-object` matching and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

⚠️ Choose the planted package so it is genuinely outside the route's graph — if you plant something already reachable, you will get a green and misread it as a passing test. Say in the report **why** the package you chose is unreachable.

⚠️ Watch for the vacuous shape: if your reachability computation silently returns "everything is reachable" (a broken traversal, a resolution failure swallowed), the gate passes on every input including the planted one. The direction-2 proof above is what catches that — do not skip it because direction 1 looked right.

### Facts on the card to re-measure rather than inherit

- The card's readings are from `7ccb53a92` and it names `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs:292` (`DEFAULT_REPORT_PATH`). ⚠️ **That file was rewritten today** by PR #6315 (card #6245) — it now has a `main(argv, env)` entry point and exported verdict constants. Re-read it on your own HEAD; the line number is certainly stale and the structure may be.
- The hand-reconstructed docs-route measurement in `registerCatalogBlocks.ts`'s header (`7738.7 kB / 29 chunks` → `9542.6 kB / 40 chunks`) is the only measurement of this budget that has ever existed and was taken once, by hand. ⛔ Do not treat it as a live number or build anything that depends on it staying true.

### Constraints

- ⛔ **Worktree-first**: `git worktree add ../objectui-6316 -b claude/issue-6316-docs-route-closure-gate main && cd ../objectui-6316 && pnpm install`.
- ⛔ **Never `git stash`** — the stack is shared across every worktree of this repo.
- ⛔ **Never touch `content/docs/releases/`.**
- ⛔ Do not set `domain:*` or type labels; file findings **unassigned**.
- ⚠️ If you wire the gate into a workflow with a `paths:` filter, **include the gate's own closure in that filter** — its YAML and the `scripts/` files it executes. That is this repo's measured convention (`half-state-patrol.yml` even lists a dependency of its script), and card #6321 exists because a gate that omits it cannot be exercised by the PR that changes it.
- Changeset required. Open the PR as **draft**; this seat arms it.

### Reporting

Structured JSON report: the gate's mechanism in two sentences, the pass on the current tree, the planted-failure proof with the RED message and why that package is unreachable, the restore evidence, and the re-measured facts where they differ from the card. If shape 2 turns out not to be implementable cheaply, ⛔ **hand back** — do not fall through to shape 1, which the ruling closed.

## Review — ACCEPT (PR #6402). The most careful instrument this lane has built today.

Reviewed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R32. Read the workflow and the wiring directly, not only the report.

### Shape 2 as ruled — and it is a gate, not a decoration

`scripts/check-docs-route-eager-closure.mjs` walks the `/docs/[[...slug]]` static module graph from **source** — route entries plus every `content/docs/**/*.mdx` module the route compiles in — and classifies each package the registrar names as **recorded payload** (11, the #4600/#4616 census, in a `MEASURED_PAYLOAD` ledger carrying no bytes and no threshold), **free** (already reachable, so a declaration and no payload), or **new graph** (fails). ⛔ No docs build, no second byte report, no ceiling constant. Checkout plus one `node` call, ~1.3 s.

⭐ **The `FREE` line turns #6314's claim into a measurement**: `@object-ui/plugin-form` and `@object-ui/plugin-grid` reachable via `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx`. The card asserted that; the gate now proves it on every run, and a refactor dropping that import flips them to new-graph — which is exactly the change that should be caught.

### ⭐ The gauge half caught a real vacuity — in this gate's own construction

> the first traversal never parsed `.mdx` files and half 3 caught it by reporting that the registrar was not on the route at all — the exact vacuity shape the dispatch warned about.

That is the whole argument for a self-judging third half, demonstrated on the instrument that contains it. A gate whose traversal silently found nothing would have passed on every input including the planted one, and looked identical to a working gate. ⛔ It also explains why the MDX half is load-bearing rather than thorough: the registrar reaches the route **only** through MDX (`schema-catalog.mdx` → `SchemaCatalogIndex` → `SchemaThumbnail`).

The `exit 2` path is the same discipline one level up: *"exit 1 is a verdict about the registrar, exit 2 says the gauge itself is not trustworthy and is never reported as the former."* An instrument that cannot measure must not report green, and must not be mistaken for a finding.

### Both directions, with the planted case argued rather than assumed

Green: 13 packages accounted for, 11 recorded, 2 free. Red: planted `@object-ui/plugin-tree` → exit 1 naming the package and the line, **while halves 2 and 3 stayed green** so the red is about the tree and not the instrument. ⭐ And the choice of plant is justified, which is the part usually skipped — `plugin-tree` is named only by `apps/console` (a different app, not on this route), and there only through a **dynamic** `registerLazy(… () => import(…))`, plus a dev-only manifest dump; `apps/site` does not depend on it and no MDX file imports it. Had it picked a package that was quietly reachable, the green would have read as a passing test.

Mutation confirmed on disk before measuring (`git hash-object` `595a019c5` → `265c75963`, plus a `grep -c` on the planted line — ⛔ never the editor's exit code). Restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with the **absolute** path, and proven: blob back to `595a019c5`, `git diff HEAD` empty, gate green again.

### The wiring is where this could have gone badly, and it did not

I checked this directly rather than on report, because the failure mode is repo-wide. Adding `Docs Route Eager Closure Check` to `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` is only safe if the check is actually **created** on every PR and every queue build — ⚠️ a required context that is never created leaves a PR *pending*, not failing, which is the trap `ci-cd-pipeline.md` already documents. Three things have to line up, and all three do:

| requirement | state |
|:--|:--|
| runs on every PR | `pull_request` on `main`/`develop`, ⛔ **no `paths:`** |
| reports on queue builds | `merge_group: types: [checks_requested]` — subscribed *from the start* |
| context name matches the list | job `name: Docs Route Eager Closure Check`, identical to the `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` string |

⭐ And the workflow says why, in its own header: *"A required check that does not report on a queue build stalls the queue until the ruleset's 60-minute timeout fails it, so an unfiltered gate that can become required subscribes here from the start."* The unfiltered choice is **load-bearing**, not tidiness.

⭐ Best of all, the property is **pinned**: `check-docs-route-eager-closure.test.ts` fails if a `paths:` or `paths-ignore:` is ever added to this workflow. Someone tidying up later cannot silently wedge the queue. That is #6321's lesson applied to a gate written the same afternoon, and the header cites #6321 for it.

### My judgement on the one thing that needed one

Adding a `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` entry widens what blocks a Dependabot auto-merge, so I checked it against the human floor rather than waving it through. It is **gate strengthening, not weakening**; it is trivially reversible; the cost is a 5-minute-timeout job with no install; and `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` is this repo's own script list, not branch protection — so this PR does not by itself make the check required in branch protection. ⛔ An unclassified blocking check is one a Dependabot merge would be let past (#6135), so **omitting** the entry would have been the riskier choice. Within this seat's remit; recording the reasoning so the decision is visible rather than assumed.

### Stale facts re-measured instead of inherited, as ordered

- `DEFAULT_REPORT_PATH` is at `check-eager-closure-budget.mjs:314` on `b116a0684`, **not `:292`** — PR #6315 moved it this afternoon. The finding it anchors is unchanged and the path is still `apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json`.
- The hand-taken `7738.7 kB / 29 chunks` figure is quoted as **history only**; nothing reads or re-takes it. ⛔ Exactly right — that number was taken once, by hand, and building on it would have made the gate depend on a measurement nobody can reproduce.

⭐ The registrar's new header corrects the misdirection that started this: *"Not `check:eager-closure`, whatever the cards that added to this list said."* #6167 and #6025 both asserted that gate governed their additions. It did not. That sentence stops the next card repeating it.

### Reported honestly rather than quietly fixed

> `check:control-bytes` went RED first, on two raw U+0000 bytes the editor materialised in the new test's absent-file sentinel; fixed by deleting the sentinel (an absent fixture file is now null) rather than escaping it.

An intermediate red, disclosed with its cause and its fix. ⛔ And fixed at the design level rather than escaped.

### Disposition

⛔ Arming on **every** check green. 27 checks on this PR — ⭐ including `Docs Route Eager Closure Check` itself, **success**, because the gate is unfiltered and therefore exercised by the PR that creates it. Four test shards, Type Check and Lint still running. Arms when clean.

## Rework round 1 — accepted. ⭐ And the full-tree instruction paid for itself immediately.

Posted by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R32.

### The red was real, and its cause was the file's existence rather than its contents

`ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` › *"gives every workflow in `.github/workflows/` its own section"* — 1 failed / 6773 passed. ⛔ Not a flake. This repo pins that page against `.github/workflows/` **in both directions**, so a new workflow with no documented section is a red by design; the pin's own message cites #3212, where `lint.yml` gated PRs for months while the page never mentioned it.

⚠️ The round-0 verification was a targeted 7-file vitest run. Well chosen for the gate itself — but **no targeted subset could have contained this pin**, because it fires on the *existence* of the new file, not on anything inside it. That is the gap, and it is worth naming as a general rule: **a PR that adds a file to a directory another gate enumerates cannot be verified by a subset chosen from the PR's own subject matter.**

### ⭐ The second pin — the one that justifies the instruction

Running the whole tree found a failure **the failing shard had never reported**:

> `merge-queue-reporting.test.ts` forbids the `## Merge Queue` section from naming any current `merge_group` subscriber outside the dated #3523 paragraph (#4154 — the page must point at `MUST_SUBSCRIBE_MERGE_GROUP`, not keep a second copy that is short by one the day the next gate lands).

The first draft named the new workflow there, as the requirable-vs-unrequirable contrast. ⭐ A second, independent staleness guard on the same page, invisible from the original failure, caught by the wider run and nothing else. Had this been fixed by clearing line 154 alone, the next push would simply have gone red somewhere new.

The repair is the right one: the Merge Queue section now teaches the **rule and the sequence** (name the context in `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` and subscribe `merge_group` in the commit that creates the workflow) while naming no file, and the contrast moved into the workflow's own section where it belongs.

### The judgement call inside the fix

⛔ The *"can never be required, structurally"* bullet was deliberately **not** extended — this workflow is the opposite case, and a claim line there would have demanded a `STRUCTURAL_BLOCKS` entry asserting something false. Checking the neighbouring assertions and then declining to satisfy one of them, with a reason, is the correct outcome; the wrong version of this round would have made every assertion mention the new file.

### Sequencing honoured

`origin/main` merged **first** (PR #6398 had landed at 20:27:53Z and edits the same page), clean, ⛔ no rebase or force-push. That is the third time this round that `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` has been the contended file, and the first time it was handled before the edit rather than after the collision.

### Verification

Full tree on `638d706b0`, clean worktree: **80 files / 2302 tests, exit 0** — with the intermediate red quoted rather than hidden (`1 failed | 79 passed`, the #4154 pin). ⭐ The gate was **re-run after the merge rather than assumed**, which matters here specifically: `packages/**` and `content/docs/**` are its own inputs, so what main brought in could have moved its verdict. It did not — 13 packages, 11 recorded, 2 free, 1349 modules from 148 route roots, 18 of 46 workspace packages still outside the closure.

Not re-run and said so: the planted-failure ablation and ESLint, since this round changed one markdown file and ESLint does not lint `content/docs`.

### Disposition

⛔ Arming on **every** check green. CI is running on `638d706b0`; four shards, Type Check and Lint outstanding. Arms when clean.
